title: Ten-mark questions
lead: Ten-mark questions ask you to use the item. Each paragraph needs a Point, Evidence, the item Applied, an Explanation and a Link back to the question. Each question has a Build, which is marked out of 10, and a Write, which gets the examiner's checklist for each paragraph and the model answer.

blocks.h: How the ten marks are earned
list: Point: a clear point that answers the question, not a definition.
Evidence: a writer, a study or a concept that fits the point.
Apply the item: quote the words of the item that show your point.
Explain: say why, what it means and so what, in that order.
Link back: end the paragraph on the words of the question.
Two paragraphs, five marks each, make ten.

qs.q: Using the item, explain how people acquire culture.
Using the item, explain how socialisation shapes identity.
Using the item, explain how socialisation in the family shapes behaviour.
Using the item, explain the role of education in socialisation.
Using the item, explain how peer groups influence identity.
Using evidence from sociological research and your own examples explain how the media acts as an agent of secondary socialisation.
Using material from the item and your knowledge, describe and explain how any two agents of socialisation influence the behaviour of children.
